text:
ava: Quick heads-up — I ran an nsys + perfetto sweep on staging after adding more NVTX ranges around the KV prefetch + batching decision points. I see a ~3% end-to-end regression and the perf timeline looks noisy near the host-side range boundaries. Posting the run notes below then a couple questions.

ava: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=staging-kvprefetch-2143456789 ./run_load_test.sh
```

ava: Quick summary from the qdrep -> summary:
- total latency (p99 synthetic trace): 12040 ms -> 12410 ms (+3.0%)
- CPU-side time spent in NVTX string formatting + push/pop: measured ~45 ms extra across 1k requests
- GPU kernel times appear unchanged, but kernel boundaries on perfetto are more fragmented so batching looks less effective in the flame

devin: thanks — can you paste the slice of the perfetto timeline where batching decision + prefetch happen? curious if the fragmentation is coming from many tiny NVTX ranges or the decision code itself.

ava: pasted a minimal copy from perfetto (simplified):
```
[host] redwood.req.9f1a2b3c:runtime.batch_decide START
[host] redwood.kv.prefetch:range START
[cuda] kernel:kv_fetch_stage_0  (20 ms)
[host] redwood.kv.prefetch:range END
[host] redwood.batch.accumulate START
[cuda] kernel:pack_tokens  (5 ms)
[host] redwood.batch.accumulate END
[host] redwood.req.9f1a2b3c:runtime.batch_decide END
```

ava: Note the host NVTX ranges are very fine-grained (prefetch start/end per keyset). With high QPS that produces a lot of short host-side ranges which show up as micro-slices in the trace.

maria: interesting. A few thoughts: 1) NVTX push/pop itself is cheap, but when we allocate formatted strings per call it adds CPU work. 2) perfetto/trace UI will show many ranges, which sometimes hides kernel-level batching because slices split kernels across trace boundaries. 3) If the batcher samples latency to decide flush, that sampling plus NVTX can interact.

devin: do we have numbers showing string formatting cost? I remember we saw this before when we used request-id interpolation into range names.

ava: yes — I instrumented host code to compare three patterns: static names, preallocated fmt with snprintf into thread-local buffer, and on-the-fly string creation. Rough numbers across 1000 requests: static names ~2 ms, snprintf ~12 ms, std::string build ~48 ms. So the worst case matches the extra ~45 ms I reported.

devin: ugh. That explains a lot. So the regression isn't GPU kernel slowdowns, it's host overhead and trace fragmentation. Two possible fixes: a) coarsen ranges (one NVTX per request or per batch instead of per key), or b) avoid per-call formatting by using small fixed tokens and attach request id in a single top-level range.

maria: Agreed. Also consider using NVTX range IDs (nvtxDomainMarkEx with integer ids) where supported, instead of long strings every time. We can map ids -> friendly names offline in trace UI if needed. That eliminates runtime formatting cost.

devin: Good call. For naming conv, propose: keep compact scope + short request id prefix. e.g.:
- runtime.req.<REQ8>.batch_decide
- runtime.kv.prefetch
- runtime.batch.accumulate
No long model/route names. That keeps strings small.

ava: +1. Example change I tested quickly: replace per-key NVTX with single `runtime.kv.prefetch` around the whole prefetch loop, and keep `runtime.req.<REQ8>` as outer. That dropped CPU overhead from 45ms->6ms and the end-to-end p99 returned to baseline within noise.

perf-bot: Automated perf regression check for staging-kvprefetch-2143456789: baseline p99 12040 ms, new p99 12110 ms (+0.58%), CI threshold 2% -> PASS. Detailed logs: /ci/perf/2143456789/report.html

ava: nice — so action items I think:
- Default instrumentation: add outer per-request NVTX named `runtime.req.<REQ8>` (8 hex chars), and coarse-grained inner ranges: `runtime.kv.prefetch`, `runtime.batch.decide`, `runtime.batch.accumulate`. Avoid per-key ranges by default.
- For debug builds we can enable fine-grain NVTX behind a flag that uses preallocated names or integer IDs.
- Update docs on NVTX naming convention + example helpers in our runtime repo (small helper that caches formatted name per thread).

maria: also add a lint in CI that fails if an NVTX call is created from an `fmt::format` or `std::string` in a hot path without being behind a debug flag. It can be a regex scan for suspicious patterns in the runtime hotpath directories.

devin: one more thought: kernel selection logic — if adding coarse NVTX hides the batching boundary in traces, we might lose visibility for debugging. Suggest a lightweight telemetry counter emitted to our tracing system (non-NVTX), e.g., incremental event counters: `kv.prefetch.count` and `batch.flush.reason` so we still have analytics without heavy trace noise.

ava: good point. I'll prototype: coarse NVTX + integer-id micro marks gated behind `RENDER_NVTX_DETAIL` env flag + counters for visibility. I'll open a small PR with the helper and updated names.

devin: sweet. If you paste the PR link I can review the perf patch and run the A/B nsys sweep.

ava: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287 — includes helper `nvtx::scoped_range_req(reqid8, name)` and CI lint.

maria: assigned review to dev and me. can you also add a note in the console docs about how we annotate traces and what to ignore when diagnosing kernel bottlenecks?

ava: will do. thanks all :+1:
